paragraphs: R. Yitzḥak ben Tavla; in chapter Taraf BaKalpi (39b): Tavlai, and in Tanḥuma, Nitzavim: Tavli. He is R. Yitzḥak Nappaḥa; he is R. Yitzḥak Ḥakula; he is R. Yitzḥak ben Elazar; he is R. Yitzḥak bar Aḥa of halakhic teachings; he is R. Yitzḥak ben Pinḥas of aggadah, chapter Arvei Pesaḥim. We may interpret this as meaning that all are names of one man, or that R. Yitzḥak Nappaḥa has four names, while R. Yitzḥak without further designation in aggadah is R. Yitzḥak ben Pinḥas, and R. Yitzḥak without further designation in halakhic teaching is R. Yitzḥak bar Aḥa. See chapter Arvei Pesaḥim (113, end of side b), whose wording is: 'He is R. Yitzḥak ben Tavla; he is R. Yitzḥak ben Ḥakula; he is R. Yitzḥak ben Ilai; he is R. Yitzḥak ben Aḥa of halakhic teachings; he is R. Yitzḥak ben Pinḥas of aggadah; your mnemonic is: Hear, please, my brothers.' Rashbam explains: 'R. Yitzḥak bar Aḥa of halakhic teachings' is a separate matter. Every R. Yitzḥak without further designation mentioned in halakhic teaching is R. Yitzḥak bar Aḥa, and R. Yitzḥak without further designation in aggadah is R. Yitzḥak ben Pinḥas. End of quotation. See for yourself that R. Yitzḥak Nappaḥa is nowhere named in this Gemara passage. There is another evident error in writing 'He is R. Yitzḥak ben Elazar,' for Mo'ed Katan (20a) has: R. Ḥiyya bar Abba, R. Ammi, and R. Yitzḥak Nappaḥa were sitting at R. Yitzḥak ben Elazar's entrance. I shall give each one a separate section. R. Yitzḥak bar Tavli, in R. Elazar's name, Shevi'it, chapter 2, halakhah 6. He asked R. Yoḥanan, Ḥanina ben Shemuel, and R. Yonah (I have forgotten its location). A case came before R. Yaakov bar Zavdi and R. Yitzḥak bar Tavli, and R. Ḥelbo said to them, Jerusalem Talmud, Niddah, chapter 2, halakhah 6. Yaakov Gevalya recited before R. Yitzḥak. R. Yitzḥak bar Tavli, in R. Shimon ben Lakish's name (see his entry). R. Shimon ben Zevid, in the name of R. Yitzḥak bar Tavli. He said, 'R. Ḥiyya Arikha said,' Nedarim (8b).
